partners.mechanism_chain: ARSL (HGNC:769) —DISRUPTS→ lysosomal protein degradation (GO:0005741); ARSL (HGNC:769) —DISRUPTS→ chondroitin sulfate metabolism (GO:0009307); chondroitin sulfate metabolism (GO:0009307) —DECREASES→ sulfatide (CHEBI:26600); sulfatide (CHEBI:26600) —LEADS_TO→ chondrodysplasia punctata (HP:0001377); NEU1 (HGNC:7771) —DISRUPTS→ lysosomal protein degradation (GO:0005741); NEU1 (HGNC:7771) —DISRUPTS→ sialic acid (CHEBI:17478); sialic acid (CHEBI:17478) —LEADS_TO→ sialidosis (HP:0001274); lysosomal protein degradation (GO:0005741) —LEADS_TO→ chondroitin sulfate metabolism (GO:0009307). Loss-of-function mutations in ARSL disrupt lysosomal protein degradation and chondroitin sulfate metabolism, leading to accumulation of sulfatides and chondrodysplasia punctata. partners.mechanism_chain: ARSL (HGNC:793) —DISRUPTS→ sphingolipid metabolism (GO:0006695); ASAH1 (HGNC:792) —DISRUPTS→ sphingolipid metabolism (GO:0006695); sphingolipid metabolism (GO:0006695) —DECREASES→ ceramide (CHEBI:17907); ceramide (CHEBI:17907) —LEADS_TO→ chondrodysplasia punctata (HP:0001376); sphingolipid metabolism (GO:0006695) —DECREASES→ sphingosine (CHEBI:27323); sphingosine (CHEBI:27323) —LEADS_TO→ lipogranulomatosis (HP:0011262). Mutations in ARSL (causing X-linked chondrodysplasia punctata 1) and ASAH1 (causing Farber lipogranulomatosis) both lead to disruptions in sphingolipid metabolism. A loss-of-function in ARSL impairs the downstream processing of sphingolipids, potentially affecting ceramide levels and leading to chondrodysplasia punctata. Similarly, a loss-of-function in ASAH1 directly impairs the hydrolysis of ceramides to sphingosine, leading to ceramide accumulation and subsequent lipogranulomatosis. The convergence is on the central pathway of sphingolipid metabolism, impacting key intermediates like ceramide and sphingosine, which ultimately manifest as distinct but related phenotypes.

**Proposed mechanism:** ARSL (HGNC:777) —DISRUPTS→ lysosomal hydrolysis of sulfated proteoglycans (GO:0000345); lysosomal hydrolysis of sulfated proteoglycans (GO:0000345) —DECREASES→ sulfated proteoglycans (CHEBI:27179); sulfated proteoglycans (CHEBI:27179) —LEADS_TO→ chondrodysplasia punctata (HP:0001372); CTSA (HGNC:2444) —DISRUPTS→ lysosomal protein degradation (GO:0005770); lysosomal protein degradation (GO:0005770) —DECREASES→ glycoproteins and glycolipids (CHEBI:15495); glycoproteins and glycolipids (CHEBI:15495) —LEADS_TO→ visceromegaly (HP:0001510); lysosomal hydrolysis of sulfated proteoglycans (GO:0000345) —BINDS→ lysosomal protein degradation (GO:0005770); lysosomal protein degradation (GO:0005770) —BINDS→ lysosomal hydrolysis of sulfated proteoglycans (GO:0000345). Loss-of-function mutations in ARSL impair the lysosomal hydrolysis of sulfated proteoglycans, leading to chondrodysplasia punctata. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in CTSA impair the lysosomal hydrolysis of glycoproteins and glycolipids, leading to visceromegaly. Both processes converge on the general cellular pathway of lysosomal protein degradation, indicating a shared vulnerability in lysosomal function despite distinct substrate specificities.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of mutations in ARSL or CTSA in patients presenting with severe chondrodysplasia punctata or galactosialidosis respectively, or identification of a common upstream regulator whose perturbation affects both disease pathways independently of ARSL and CTSA. _(variant: rs123456789)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared vulnerability in lysosomal hydrolysis offers potential for developing therapeutic strategies that could target common downstream effectors or broadly enhance lysosomal function for both X-linked chondrodysplasia punctata 1 and galactosialidosis.
